SVT with Aberrancy

Level: Advanced Topic: Cardiology, ECG, EMS/Critical Care Duration: Deep Dive

Arrival Scenario

You respond to an “unstable tachycardia.” The monitor: wide QRS tach (>160), no p waves, borderline hypotensive. “Is it VT or SVT with aberrancy?” Your answer determines whether you shock, block, or both—what are your decision criteria?

Warm-Up Questions

  1. What ECG features favor VT over SVT with aberrancy?
  2. Name two historical findings that argue for SVT.
  3. Which medications are never given if you’re unsure?
  4. Why is “capture/fusion” beat a can’t-miss clue?
  5. When is adenosine both a diagnostic and therapeutic tool?

Optional Tally Embed

Explanation / Breakdown

Key ECG Clues

  • VT (Ventricular Tach):
    • History: Old, h/o structural heart, infarct
    • Wide QRS (>140 ms), AV dissociation (independent p waves), fusion/capture beats, all positive/negative QRS in precordials, extreme axis
  • SVT with aberrancy:
    • H/o young, no heart disease, sudden onset/offset, response to vagal/adenosine

Treatment

  • If unstable: SHOCK first
  • If stable, likely SVT: Adenosine challenge (if wide IRREGULAR, never)
  • NEVER give Ca-channel or adenosine if unsure/suspect pre-excite (afib+WPW) or wide-irregular

Common Mistakes

  • Delaying shock in true VT; most patients tolerate SVT better
  • Administering AV nodal blocks to wide, irregular, or undifferentiated tachyarrhythmias
  • Missing fusion/capture as the best proof of VT

Clinical Pearls

  • When in doubt, shock the unstable or undifferentiated wide tach
  • Try adenosine ONLY if regular stable wide, not known to be VT, and not irregular
  • VT is much more common than SVT with aberrancy in adults (>90%)
  • Always reassess for recurrence, especially after vagal/adenosine

Decision Trees

Is it VT or SVT with Aberrancy?

  1. History structural heart dz? QRS >0.14s?
    • Yes → Likely VT
  2. Response to vagal/adenosine?
    • Yes → SVT
  3. Irregular wide?
    • Don’t treat as SVT; avoid nodal blockers

Practice Cases

Case 1: Elderly, Prior MI

  • 68M, palpitations, wide QRS tach, fusion beats visible, unresponsive to vagal.

    What’s the rhythm? Treatment?

Case 2: Youth, No Heart Hx

  • 22F, sudden palpitations, 160s, reg wide QRS, converts with adenosine.

    SVT or VT?

Reflection

  • How do you confirm if you got it right, and what’s your “second opinion plan” if you’re unsure?
  • When would you push for immediate ED/cardiology consult in the field?
